item.text:
Refactored the design by collapsing the hidden implementation layer into [MinHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:4) and deleting `IntBinaryHeap.java`. For a codebase this small, the separate facade-plus-core split had become mostly delegation overhead. `MinHeap` now owns its storage and heap mechanics directly, while `IntHeap` and `LegacyMinHeapApi` remain as the actual API boundaries.

This keeps the design simpler without changing behavior: constructors, bulk loading, indexed updates, root replacement, and heap maintenance now live in one cohesive class instead of bouncing through an internal wrapper. The public and legacy interfaces still work the same, but there’s less indirection and less code to keep in sync.
